# --instructions--

Complete the class-based enumeration `Level`: add a `constructor(name, value)` that stores both arguments in the properties `name` and `value` and freezes the instance, the `static` members `LOW`, `MEDIUM` and `HIGH`, each built with its own name as a string and the values `1`, `2` and `3`, and a `static values()` method that returns the three members in that order

# --asserts--

`Level.LOW` must be an instance of `Level`.

```javascript
tryCatch(Level.LOW instanceof Level);
```

`Level.HIGH.name` must be `"HIGH"` and `Level.HIGH.value` must be `3`.

```javascript
tryCatch(Level.HIGH.name === "HIGH" && Level.HIGH.value === 3);
```

`Level.MEDIUM.value` must be `2`.

```javascript
tryCatch(Level.MEDIUM.value === 2);
```

`Level.values()` must return `[Level.LOW, Level.MEDIUM, Level.HIGH]`.

```javascript
tryCatch(JSON.stringify(Level.values()) === JSON.stringify([Level.LOW, Level.MEDIUM, Level.HIGH]) && Level.values()[0] === Level.LOW && Level.values()[2] === Level.HIGH);
```

Every member must be frozen.

```javascript
tryCatch(Object.isFrozen(Level.LOW) && Object.isFrozen(Level.MEDIUM) && Object.isFrozen(Level.HIGH));
```

# --solutions--

```javascript
class Level {
  static LOW = new Level("LOW", 1);
  static MEDIUM = new Level("MEDIUM", 2);
  static HIGH = new Level("HIGH", 3);

  constructor(name, value) {
    this.name = name;
    this.value = value;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }

  static values() {
    return [Level.LOW, Level.MEDIUM, Level.HIGH];
  }
}
Object.freeze(Level);
```
